args.sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT o.store_id, o.customer, COUNT(*) n FROM orders o WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT s.name, COUNT(*) customers, MEDIAN(n) med, (SELECT MAX(ordered_at) FROM orders) mx FROM c LEFT JOIN stores s ON c.store_id=s.id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE customer IS NULL), COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE store_id IS NULL) FROM orders WHERE ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND ordered_at < '2026-01-01'

args.message: Brooklyn had the highest median: 701 customers ordered there in 2025, with a median of 167 orders each. Philadelphia (158) and Chicago (157) came next, then San Francisco (146). New Orleans (70, opened April 2025) and Los Angeles (24, opened October 2025) are low because they were only open for part of the year. I counted orders per customer per store for orders placed in calendar year 2025. A customer who ordered at more than one store is counted at each of them. No 2025 orders were missing a customer or a store.
